```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness to pay is better evidenced in A. One sourced quote shows a founder already paying for bookkeeping ('I hired someone. It costs a lot'). Another quantifies a recurring 3-4 hours a month of pain. B's demand quotes show anxiety, not payment, and its strongest payment-related quote describes substituting a general ChatGPT subscription rather than paying for a dedicated tool.",
    "A's need recurs every month. B's need, by its own admission, mostly ends at re-employment, which caps lifetime value and forces constant new-customer acquisition.",
    "A's price anchors ($29-100/mo, from Kick and FlexedLedger) are about 3-4x B's ($8-24/mo). That leaves more room to absorb acquisition costs, and fewer customers are needed to show traction within 90 days.",
    "A has a sourced, low-cash channel through the Stripe App Marketplace, which reaches users who already have the exact Stripe reconciliation problem. B's sourced Google Search channel costs $62-118 per lead against a sub-$25/mo price. B's cheaper Meta channel (~$12.30 per lead) has an unverified conversion rate.",
    "Both niches are crowded with free tiers, so saturation does not separate them. A's narrower wedge (pure Stripe-to-bank reconciliation) is mechanical and rules-based, a good fit for AI agents. B's 'trajectory advice' on sensitive gaps (health, caregiving) carries harm and reputational risk under light supervision.",
    "Counterweight: A carries a heavier trust and security burden, since SOC2 is commercially expected and Plaid/Stripe terms need review. However, A's brief says SOC2 is not legally required to launch, so it slows enterprise-grade trust more than a first paying customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B uses the every.to quote ('I don't have $100–$150 per hour to spend on a career coach... but I do have a subscription to ChatGPT') to illustrate willingness to pay for cheap AI career tools. It actually shows a user meeting the need with a general-purpose LLM they already pay for, which undercuts demand for a paid standalone gap tool. A close second: one of B's two price anchors (WeGoUp at $9.99/mo) comes from a product described as pre-alpha, so it does not show that anyone pays that price.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs show saturated markets with free competitors, and neither provides conversion data. A's own evidence has gaps. The Growthy figure of $400-600/mo in bookkeeper time per client has no link, so it is treated as unsourced. The brief also describes Kick's free tier inconsistently: '250 txns/yr' in one place and '$25K/mo expenses' in another. The pick rests mainly on recurring need, higher price points, sourced evidence of existing spend, and the Stripe Marketplace channel, not on any proven path to a first sale."
}
```
